lines: Two of the six came back to be let out. Grown men who own coats, stood sheepish in my doorway.
I let them out and I charged them for it. They were glad to pay for something ordinary.
The other four are being worn. Nobody up here has ever been sorry to own a coat.
Six coats ordered in a fortnight, and four of them for grown men who own coats.
They are not cold. They are getting ready for something and they cannot say what.
The loom pays for the winter, and the winter is when there is time to weave.
It sounds like a trap when you say it out loud. It is actually a very good deal.
Everyone here can weave and everyone here says they cannot. It is a thing they do.
Mum says this town has one skill and eleven hundred people pretending they lack it.
